I'll point each agent to the prior AC-security-audit.md to avoid duplicate findings, and instruct them to avoid devhost/edits, output ranked findings with file:line, exploit trace, suggested fix, and a failing test, keeping the report under 900 words.

input.description: Security audit A: SSO + Platform API
input.prompt:
READ-ONLY security re-audit of new Cyrus surfaces in the git worktree /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r49 (Next.js + Prisma). Do NOT edit any file, do NOT run /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost, npm, tsc, tests, builds or servers; only read code (cat/grep/sed). Never touch /opt/nxeon. First skim /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/AC-security-audit.md (the FIRST audit; do not re-report its findings unless still open) and /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/AG-bridge.md + AI-bridge-api.md.

Scope A: (1) r36 SSO + domain mode: middleware.ts, lib/cyrus/bridge/{config,routing,flow,assertion,assertion-rules}.ts, lib/cyrus-bridge/server.ts, app/sso/cyrus/**, app/cyrus-host/**, lib/auth.ts changes, app/login/page.tsx. (2) r38 Platform API + grants: app/api/platform/cyrus/** (v1/[...path], grants, webhooks), lib/nxeon-platform/** (api, grants, scopes, servers, entitlements, events, watch, server-tokens), lib/cyrus/host/platform*.ts, app/dashboard/connect/cyrus/page.tsx, components/platform/ConnectCyrusForm.tsx, app/api/cyrus/platform-events/route.ts, app/api/cyrus/purchase-events/route.ts, app/api/cyrus/v1/purchase-events/route.ts, app/api/cyrus/install-report/route.ts.

Hunt for: open redirect, host-header / x-forwarded-host trust, header-marker spoofing, cookie scope/flags, CSRF on state-changing routes, signature/HMAC verification (timing-safe compare, canonicalisation, replay windows, nonce/jti reuse), IDOR (server id / grant id / user id not bound to the caller), scope checks per Platform API operation (e.g. file write with read-only grant, path traversal / allow-list bypass in file primitives incl. symlinks, '..', encoded paths, absolute paths), revoked-grant window abuse, rate-limit keys forgeable, error messages leaking secrets, fail-open when env/flag is missing, impersonation crossing hosts, suspended users still acting.

Output (under 900 words): ranked findings (High/Medium/Low) each with: file:line, a concrete exploit trace (request sequence), confidence, minimal fix, and a sketch of a failing unit test (which existing test file + what to assert; look at test/cyrus-bridge-*.test.ts and test/cyrus-platform*.test.ts for patterns). Then a short list "checked and OK". Then "owner decisions" (policy choices, not bugs). Be precise; false positives waste the owner's money, so verify each by reading the actual code path end to end.

content.content:
## Rules that never relax
Fail closed on unknown state (tokens, entitlements, plan, flags). Real servers only through Test Flight; never a customer server. Sound audio never in git or served raw. Game-derived material never public. No secret in d

## r32 findings: fixed (all with tests)
| # | Sev | Area | Finding | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AC-1 | MED | API v1 | a client with its own subject key could sign `sub=<any Nxeon user id>` | `CYRUS_API_V1_IDENTITY_CLIENTS` (default `nxeon`); others get 403 `subject_not_allowed` |
| AC-2 | MED | meshgen scratch | driver expressions bypassed the static scan and reached Blender's eval (proven on node-2) | scan covers driver expressions; scratch remains OFF |
| AC-3 | MED | designer Java | Javadoc/unicode-escape injection through names | `javadocText()` sanitises; also config exporter |
| AC-4 | MED | Mod Packs | pack create/install skipped networking consent and the Test Flight gate | `memberInstallGate()` on create, conflicts and every install |
| AC-5 | MED | library reports | one account could mass-hold assets with copyright reports | 5 legal auto-holds per reporter per 24 h, then 3 reporters needed |
| AC-6 | LOW-MED | library takedown | stored near-copies stayed published | takedown holds every published `duplicateOf` copy |
| AC-7 | MED (latent) | host HTTP server | a leaked host key could write any platform setting; body buffered before size check | writes limited to `cyrus_` keys; oversize refused before reading |
| AC-8 | LOW | Test Flight | `\r` not stripped in `server.properties` values | strip CR, LF, NUL, U+2028/2029/0085 |
| AC-9 | LOW | data packs | a command ending in `\` joins the next entry (1.20.2+) | refused (`line_continuation`) |

## r32 findings: open (status as of the last update)
| # | Sev | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| O-1 | LOW | telemetry ingest: HMAC over body only, no timestamp/nonce, whole body buffered | **closed in r40** (telemetry v2: timestamp + single-use batch, capped stream, IP limit) |
| O-2 | LOW | AI gateway tokens never expire | **closed in r40** (max age) |
| O-3 | LOW | Server Doctor audit-row failures swallowed | open (owner: fail closed or alert) |
| O-4 | LOW | Test Flight log-matcher regexes can backtrack | open (bounded by the runner's kill timeout; RE2 later) |
| O-5 | LOW | pack install/uninstall loop could restart a user's own server about once a minute; in-memory limiter | open (per-server restart budget N/hour is an owner number) |
| O-6 | LOW | no per-user Mod Pack count/byte quota; no create idempotency | open (owner: quota numbers) |
| O-7 | INFO | delivery Idempotency-Key not bound to the body | open (hash body into key) |
| O-8 | LOW | library filters are text-only (no NFKC/confusables, no pixel/audio classifier) | open (hold first-time contributors for review, or a classifier) |
| O-9 | LOW | import licence claim accepted as typed | open (manual review before any public share; public sharing is hard-off) |
| O-10 | INFO | hosted packs are public by sha1 (capability URL, no expiry) | open (owner: OK as public or signed URLs) |
| O-11 | LOW | API v1 replay caches are in-process (50k cap) | open (shared store before more than one instance) |
| O-12 | INFO | the host key is full trust for reads | by design |
| O-13 | - | meshgen kernel-escape untested | open (microVM/gVisor before `CYRUS_MESHGEN_SCRATCH`) |

Not read end to end by the audit: Test Flight `runner.js`, playtest `bot.js`, `telemetry/collect.ts`, library `stage-b/c.ts`, admin library routes. Later features (r36 SSO has its own review; r38 Platform API; r40 admin)

## Owner security decisions pending (from the r32 list)
Kodely identity policy for API v1; whether networking mods may be bundled into packs; copyright-report rules; per-server restart budget; Mod Pack quotas; build service must leave the subscription login for an API key wit

| R49-2 | MED | Platform API | restart budget checked before the lock and counted only audited calls: parallel requests all passed | **fixed**: checked inside the per-server lock + in-flight count; a revoked op gets one rollback restart |
| R49-3 | MED | Platform API | revoked-grant rollback window allowed reads of any file, inventory, logs, and skipped the "still your server" check | **fixed**: rollback reads only the op's own paths; inventory/logs refused; ownership checked always. `setPack` in rollback still accepts any URL (open, owner) |

| R49-7 | MED | conversions | consent age never checked (180-day rule) | **fixed** (old/future consent sends nothing). A consent WITHDRAWN without a new sign-in is still not pushed to the server: open, owner |
| R49-8 | MED | BYO / library | game-derived marker could be dropped by saving the same pixels under a new key without a base | **fixed**: marker is sticky by key and by vanilla pixel hash. A slightly edited vanilla texture is not caught (look-alike check at contribution: owner) |
| R49-9 | MED | admin tokens | BILLING staff could rewrite the token economy (metering off, tokens per $) with no range checks | **fixed**: ADMIN (platform area) + the catalog's min/max validation |
| R49-10 | MED | notifications | a second takedown of the same target was dropped as a duplicate | **fixed**: one notice per takedown action |
| R49-11 | LOW | tokens | cumulative partial refunds (50% then 60%) could take back 100% | **fixed** (prior revokes subtracted, like the Stripe path) |
| R49-12 | LOW | SSO | `__Host-` cookies were "deleted" without `Secure` (browsers ignore it) | **fixed** for the SSO state and Cyrus session cookies |
| open | LOW | Platform API | `inventory.read` can read any file under plugins/mods/config + `server.properties` (rcon password, bot tokens) | owner: narrow + redact |
| open | LOW | Platform API | suspended users still act through it; `server.reload` deny-list; raw host errors returned | backlog |
| open | LOW | admin | audit write failures swallowed (after the change); `setting.set` confirm inverted for risky-off keys; SUPPORT can suspend an ADMIN's Cyrus | backlog / owner |
| open | LOW | tokens | server-grant reversal only on the admin Refund (not Stripe-dashboard refunds/disputes); 150-token minimum for any paid order | owner numbers |
| open | LOW | keys / exports | key creation without step-up, `expiryDays:0` = never; expired export unlink can orphan a zip; dev foundation allows any non-production NODE_ENV and the whole preview list | backlog / owner |
| open | LOW | build queue | per-account cap (2 in flight) is count-then-create (a burst can pass it); the service queue is FIFO | backlog |

'''
s=s.replace(a, sec+a,1)
open(p,"w").write(s)
EOF

Dev note: run `next dev -H localhost` (with `-H 127.0.0.1` Next treats the rewrite as an external proxy).

content.thinking:
In the second run, sign-up and both SSO passed, but logout hit a page timeout and the wallet test failed because the APIRequestContext bypasses Chromium's host resolver rules—it resolved nxeon.cloud through real DNS to the production primary IP on port 4148, which then timed out.

The fix is to stop using page.request for fake hosts and instead run fetch calls via page.evaluate from within the page itself, so cookies and same-origin context carry over properly; cross-host API key calls should use credentials: 'omit'. This confirms it: the __Host- cookies for SSO state aren't being stored over plain http on next, so SSO flows won't work there. I need another approach — either accept SSO can't run on next (not acceptable) or set up a local TLS terminator with Playwright configured to ignore HTTPS errors via an https proxy.

I'm thinking through a small Node https proxy on node-2 with a self-signed cert forwarding to the app port, so origins become https://nxeon.cloud:8443 and https://cyrus.my:8443, making Secure cookies and CSP upgrades work without any bypass hacks. I'd write this as a committed `.qa/tls-proxy.mjs` script implementing a simple proxy that pipes requests via http.request, preserves the Host header, and adds x-forwarded-proto https, then restart next with updated APP_URL/CYRUS_ORIGIN env vars pointing to the new https port (using a shifted port like PORT+1000=5148 to avoid collisions) and COOKIE_SECURE enabled by default.

Since the rate limiter reads client IP from the proxy connection, every request will appear as 127.0.0.1 — that's acceptable for this setup.

input.title: Stop shipping all of simple-icons on every dashboard page
input.tldr: A lab performance run of the Cyrus customer app found one 5 MB (about 2 MB gzipped) JavaScript chunk on every /dashboard page: the whole simple-icons set, pulled in by the "heard about us" prompt in the dashboard layout. The new session swaps the namespace import for named imports and checks the bundle shrinks.
input.prompt:
Nxeon portal performance bug (found by the Cyrus r49 QA lab run, 2026-10-11): every page under /dashboard downloads one ~5 MB raw / ~2 MB gzipped JS chunk that is the ENTIRE `simple-icons` package (3,300+ brand icons). Cause: `components/customer/HeardAboutUsPrompt.tsx` is a "use client" component rendered by `app/dashboard/layout.tsx`, and it does `import * as simpleIcons from "simple-icons"` and then looks icons up dynamically: `(simpleIcons as Record<string, unknown>)[entry.key]` (line ~40). A dynamic key defeats tree-shaking, so the whole package lands in the client bundle.
